$comment: THE declared support set. Every target Kibitz claims to support is a
row here, and this file — not the build matrix — decides what a
release must contain. The matrix is generated from it and the release
is verified against it, so a target cannot be built without being
required, or required without being built.
Why it lives outside the workflow: on 2026-08-01 the matrix carried a
comment stating that every entry must name its own bundles, in a
matrix that had no Windows entry at all. The rule was correct and the
enumeration it described was incomplete, so it validated only the
members already present. A guard derived from the same list it is
meant to police repeats that. Adding a platform means adding it HERE,
`requires` are globs matched against the collected artifacts; every
one must be present or the release refuses to publish. Architecture is
part of a target, not a detail of one: macOS ships two DMGs because an
Intel Mac cannot run the Apple Silicon build.
